_castCeilings_what: A literal cast to a real type is a fake the compiler has been told not to check. Every one of these types ALREADY has a builder in tests/helpers, so the target for each is ZERO and the number may only fall. Seeded 2026-08-31 from a measurement of 1,735 literal-casts across the test tree; these nine are the ones with a builder standing right next to them.
_logger_closed: CLOSED 2026-09-01. Seeded at 296 hand-rolled logger fakes; the last four were converted the same day (two EDS service suites, one rate-limiting suite whose fake is read inside a jest.mock factory, and one handler testUtils). The list stays as an EMPTY ARRAY rather than being deleted because the two tests below read it: one bans a new hand-rolled fake outright, the other fails on a stale row. With the array empty the first is a flat ban.
_castBans_what: Families whose OBJECT-LITERAL casts reached zero. Read the scope precisely: the check is brace-anchored (`} as T`), so it bans a hand-rolled LITERAL standing in for T — the thing a builder replaces. It does NOT ban every `as T`. Measured by AST on 2026-09-01, casts of other expressions to these types remain: Logger 98, StateManager 63, CommandExecutor 9, ExtensionContext 0. Those are a different defect with a different fix (an argument cast is a silenced type error, not a missing builder) and are tracked by `astTotals` below, not by these bans. Entries are never removed.

astTotals._what: Every `as T` anywhere in tests/, counted on the SYNTAX TREE by scripts/codemod/survey-casts.mjs — not the brace-anchored regex the ceilings use. Recorded 2026-09-01 because the two numbers differ a lot and reporting the smaller one as if it were the whole picture overstated what the bans achieved.
